references.text: Parallel text where God answers that none of the men who saw his glory and the signs in Egypt and in the wilderness, yet tested him ten times and did not listen to him, shall see the land he promised their fathers.
God declares that all those numbered from twenty years old and upward, who grumbled against him, shall fall in the wilderness and not enter the land.
Moses recounts how the Lord was angry when he heard the people's words, and swore that none of the men of this evil generation should see the good land he had promised their fathers.
God's promise to Abraham to give the land to his offspring, referred to in the phrase 'the land which I swore to give to Abraham'.
God's promise to Isaac to give him and his offspring all these lands, and to confirm the oath he swore to Abraham.
God's promise to Jacob to give him and his offspring the land on which he lies, which is the promise given to Abraham and Isaac.
Reference to the oath God swore to Abraham, Isaac, and Israel to give the land to their offspring forever.

Moses reminds the people that the Lord has set the land before them, and that they shall go in and take possession of it, the land which the Lord swore to give to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob and their offspring.
The psalm refers to the wilderness generation who wandered in their hearts and did not know God's ways, and God's oath that they should not enter his rest.

Hebrews cites the unbelief of the wilderness generation as an example, pointing to those against whom God was angry for forty years, those who sinned and fell in the wilderness, and who were not allowed to enter because of unbelief.
